title: Response Figure Averaged across a Run of Met Superhost Assessments (Host Accounts)
content:
# Desk Guidance — Response Figure of a Superhost Decision (Host Accounts)

For an individual Host Accounts holder whose Superhost assessment is decided again, the decision's response figure depends on how many of the account's Superhost assessments dated within the 12 months before the decision were recorded as met.

## Rule

| Superhost assessments dated within the 12 months before the decision recorded as met | The decision's response figure |
|---|---|
| 3 or more | The average of the response rates of **all** of the account's Superhost assessments dated within the 12 months before the decision |
| 1 or 2 | The same average over the assessments dated within the **6 months** before the decision |
| None | No other assessment is averaged in: the figure is the decided assessment's response rate |

In each average, the decided assessment counts at the response rate the decision takes for that assessment, in place of the rate recorded on it, and every other assessment counts at its recorded response rate. Each average is rounded half up to 2 decimal places.

A window of a number of months holds the records dated fewer than that many whole calendar months before the date of the decision.

## Worked averages (hypothetical accounts)

**Three met in the 12 months.** Within the 12 months the account has four Superhost assessments: three recorded as met with response rates of 88.00%, 92.00% and 95.00%, and the decided assessment, whose rate taken for the decision is 86.00%. The figure is 88.00, 92.00, 95.00 and 86.00 averaged: 361.00 divided by 4, which is **90.25%**.

**One met in the 12 months.** Only one assessment within the 12 months was recorded as met. Within the 6 months before the decision there are two assessments: one at 91.00% and the decided assessment at 87.00%. The figure is **89.00%**.

**None met.** The figure is the decided assessment's response rate alone.

## Points of judgement

- The count of met assessments looks at the 12-month window even when the average itself runs over 6 months.
- All assessments in the window are averaged — met and not met alike — once the count of met assessments has been settled.
